facts.text: In 1796, Spanish Governor Baron de Carondelet ordered a fort built at the Black River–Mississippi confluence, founding what would become Minorca.
The Mississippi state line, following a former channel of the Mississippi River, is directly north of Minorca.
Geographically, Minorca occupies a flat, alluvial plain typical of the Mississippi Delta region, supporting agriculture and proximity to transportation routes like U.S.
At 56 feet above sea level, Minorca's flat terrain—never rising more than 59 feet within two miles—makes it prone to flooding.
The Minorca Cemetery holds graves from the late 1800s and early 1900s, including Reverend Elijah Kernall (1848–1913).
During Reconstruction, the Minorca Plantation became a focal point for free labor arrangements under the Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands.
